Note on Fed Funds: the FRED endpoint was blocked in this environment, so no Fed Funds series exists in the dataset. The scoring model uses a yield-based proxy (13-week bill + TLT trend), not actual Fed Funds. This row is intentionally left unavailable and links to the authoritative FRED series for verification.

Source Verification Links

Open the provider page to independently verify each value. Yahoo quote pages use the caret symbols; FRED series are provided as macro cross-checks.

Definition caveatThe dashboard's Yield Curve is 10Y − 13W (^TNX − ^IRX), while FRED T10Y2Y is 10Y − 2Y. They are different spreads — the FRED link is a cross-check, not the exact input used by the score.

Welcome — start here

This dashboard works out of the box. You do not need to know Python, command prompts, web servers, or computer code. Pick a date, press Generate Score, and read the result. Everything you see is explained in plain language below.

  1. Choose any date in the Date Explorer tab (or press Generate Latest Score).
  2. Press Generate Score. A number from 0 to 100 appears with a plain-English label.
  3. Use the other tabs to compare dates, explore history, or check where each number came from.

If live market quotes are unavailable, the dashboard automatically uses its built-in historical dataset. Nothing is broken and no action is needed.

Ways to open this dashboard, ranked by simplicity

You only need ONE of these. Option 1 is the easiest if a hosted link is available.

1

Use the hosted GitHub Pages version Easiest · recommended

Just open a web link — like opening any website. Nothing to install, works on phones and tablets, and live market data normally works there too. Ask the person who shared this file for the hosted link.

I publish these files — how do I set up GitHub Pages?
  1. Create a GitHub repository and upload index.html (the file is self-contained — that is all GitHub Pages needs).
  2. In the repository, open Settings → Pages.
  3. Under Build and deployment → Source, choose Deploy from a branch, select main and /(root), then press Save.
  4. Wait about 1–2 minutes, then open the github.io link GitHub shows you. Bookmark it and share it.

To update the hosted version later, replace index.html in the repository with the new one. The link stays the same.

2

Double-click Launch Dashboard.bat / Launch Dashboard.cmd Windows · easy

On a Windows computer, double-click the launcher file. Both extensions work the same way — use whichever one is present in your folder. It starts a private local web server and opens the dashboard in your browser automatically. You do not need to type anything.

  1. Keep the launcher (.bat or .cmd) in the same folder as ETF_Timing_Dashboard.html and index.html.
  2. Double-click Launch Dashboard.bat — or Launch Dashboard.cmd if that is the file you received.
  3. The dashboard opens by itself. A small background window keeps it working — close that window when you are finished.

If Windows shows a blue "Windows protected your PC" screen, click More info → Run anyway (this is a text file that only opens a browser on your own computer).

3

Manual local server Advanced users only

You do not need this option for normal use — Options 1 and 2 are simpler. It is listed only for developers who already have a technical setup.

Show advanced command (not required)

From this folder, run python -m http.server 8000 then open http://localhost:8000/. This is purely optional.

Plain-language troubleshooting

I see "Live market quotes are currently unavailable"Nothing to fix. The dashboard is using its built-in historical data dated 2026-11-13. All tabs and scores still work.
Charts are blankThe chart library is loaded from the internet. Connect to the internet and reload, or use the hosted version. Scores and tables still work without it.
The banner says I am running from my computerYou opened the file directly. Press Continue with embedded data for a fully offline experience, or use Option 1 / Option 2 above to enable live quotes.
I need help with a numberOpen the Market Data Audit tab. It shows exactly where each value came from and on which date it was observed.
